The codebase's own convention - services/groups.ts throws 'a system group and cannot be deleted' / 'Membership is maintained automatically; it cannot be edited' - should hold for every writer, including SCIM-in group PUT/PATCH/DELETE and member operations. SCIM clients should receive a 400 mutability error for system groups, matching how RFC 7644 mutability is already used at memberStatements:592 for dynamic (rule) groups.

trace.description: PATCH on the watchlist group id passes requireScope(directory:write) - no admin scope needed - and reaches the member/displayName op loop at 645-670.
DELETE on the watchlist group id: loadGroup(c, true) passes because 'Risk watchlist' is not an admin-role group; the only delete guard is the name check at :680 which also misses.
The single choke point for group writes checks `group.name === SUPER_ADMINS_GROUP || adminRoleGroupIds` (line 523) but never `group.system` - the system flag the service layer treats as untouchable.

Membership-write statements are built with only a `group.rule` (dynamic-group) refusal at :592 and an admin-member scope check at :594-597; system groups flow straight through to DELETE/INSERT on group_members at :599-601.

Outbound group sync enumerates ALL groups with no system filter, so forged watchlist membership/name reaches every SCIM target; PATCH additionally calls pushGroupAndRemoved immediately via downstream().

scimDeprovisionStatements('group') queues a remote delete for every SCIM target linked to the group, then group_members and the groups row itself are deleted (or member rows replaced on PATCH/PUT) - the system group's integrity is destroyed locally and its tampered state is pushed downstream.

evidence.description: loadGroup write guard covers only SUPER_ADMINS_GROUP name and adminRoleGroupIds - `group.system` is not consulted anywhere in scim-server.ts (grep for 'system' finds only unrelated hits).

Service-layer invariant the SCIM path bypasses: '"..." is a system group and cannot be deleted.' Also :174/:190 'Membership ... is maintained automatically; it cannot be edited.' and :207 'it takes no managers.'
watchlistGroup() selects `WHERE system = 'watchlist'` - the group is internal machinery keyed by the system flag, its members are a mirror of user_watch (flagUser inserts at :360).

reconcileWatchlist rebuilds group_members from user_watch only inside sweepWatchlist (hourly cron, :385-395) - tampered membership persists and is pushed downstream until then, and reconcile early-returns when the group was deleted.
syncGroups pushes `SELECT * FROM groups` (no `system = ''` filter), so the tampered watchlist group state propagates to every configured SCIM target.
Access-governance request path refuses system groups ('is maintained by the system - its membership cannot be requested') - a third writer honoring the same invariant.

conditions.description: Caller needs a SCIM API key with the directory:write scope - the standard credential handed to external provisioning integrations; no admin scope or console session is required.

The deployment must use the Cloudflare One integration enough for the watchlist group to exist (created lazily on first flagUser), or value any other future groups.system marker. Downstream impact additionally requires at least one SCIM target configured (or a consumer reading /scim/v2/Groups).
Members injected via SCIM must resolve to existing users by external_id (memberIds resolves scim user links / external_id) and must not hold an admin role (admin members require admin scope at :555).

execution.attacker_perspective: Holder of a directory:write-scoped SCIM API key (external provisioning integration) - a delegated, non-admin trust tier.
payloads: PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/<watchlist-id> {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"replace","path":"members","value":[{"value":"<victim-scim-id>"}]}]}
PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/<watchlist-id> {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"replace","path":"displayName","value":"Terminated employees"}]}
DELETE /scim/v2/Groups/<watchlist-id>
instructions: GET /scim/v2/Groups?filter=displayName eq "Risk watchlist" (directory:read) to learn the group id, or enumerate all groups.
PATCH members replace with attacker-chosen member values; observe 200 and an immediate outbound push (pushGroupAndRemoved via downstream()).

On each SCIM target, the 'Risk watchlist' group now contains the chosen users (or is empty) until the hourly reconcileWatchlist restores the user_watch-derived set; repeat the PATCH to sustain the forged state.
Alternatively DELETE the group: the local row and all member rows are removed and a remote deprovision is queued for each linked target.
execution.observed_result: The watchlist system group accepts directory:write mutations - membership replacement, rename, deletion - that every non-SCIM writer refuses; forged membership is pushed to outbound SCIM targets within the request's downstream() drain and persists until the hourly sweep re-derives membership from user_watch.

remediation.strategy: Extend the existing mutability guard to system groups at the single choke point: in loadGroup, when write is true and group.system is non-empty, throw a ScimError(400, mutability) the same way memberStatements already refuses dynamic (rule) groups - or delegate group writes to services/groups.ts which already enforces the invariant. POST /scim/v2/Groups may also refuse creating groups that collide with reserved system-group names to avoid duplicate-name confusion downstream.

likelihood.reason: Any directory:write SCIM key suffices - these are delegated to external HR/provisioning systems precisely so they can manage groups; a curious or hostile integration operator needs only a group id, which directory:read discloses.

impact.reason: Corrupts a security-signal group that propagates to connected SCIM targets (forged 'risky' memberships, stripped real ones, or full group deprovisioning downstream); bounded by hourly self-heal and confined to the group plane - user_watch, CF lists, and admin-role guards are unaffected.

confidence.reason: Source-verified end to end: the missing system check, the write paths that reach it, the outbound propagation, and the self-healing bound are all in code; no runtime dependency needed beyond what the schema guarantees.

title: POST /api/v1/setup stores unbounded app_name/login_subtitle: runSetup calls the raw setters, skipping the APP_NAME_MAX/SUBTITLE_MAX validation every other write path enforces
description: The branding write paths bound app_name to 60 chars and login_subtitle to 140 (saveAppName/saveLoginSubtitle in src/services/settings.ts:286-296, enforced for PATCH /api/v1/branding, the console, and per-domain brands). runSetup instead calls lib-level setAppName/setLoginSubtitle directly (src/services/setup.ts:142-149), so POST /api/v1/setup with app_name of any length stores it; every page response then re-emits the oversized name ~4x (title, brand, footer, CSP-bearing pages). A caller needs the settings:write legacy scope - a conjunction of security+branding+email+scim+schemas write - or the bootstrap token, so the trust tier is high; the gap is a validation bypass of the same root-cause family as the fixed 'branding.patch.unbounded-name-subtitle' record.
root_cause: src/services/setup.ts:143/147 call setAppName(env, ...) / setLoginSubtitle(env, ...) (src/lib/settings.ts:301-314), which store the value verbatim - the length caps live one layer up in src/services/settings.ts and are skipped.
intended_behavior: All writers of app_name/login_subtitle should go through the bounded service functions (or validate identically), as the fixed PATCH path now does.

trace.description: Setup route admitted by the settings:write legacy scope or the bootstrap token.
Calls raw setters, not saveAppName/saveLoginSubtitle.
setSetting stores the raw value; getAppName/getLoginSubtitle echo it into every rendered page.

evidence.description: `await setAppName(env, String(body.app_name));` - raw lib call.
saveAppName throws over APP_NAME_MAX (60); the cap the setup path skips.
APP_NAME_MAX = 60, SUBTITLE_MAX = 140.

conditions.description: Caller holds the settings:write legacy scope (which expands to security+branding+email+scim+schemas write) or the bootstrap token pre-completion.

execution.attacker_perspective: A broad delegated settings:write key (already holding branding:write among its conjunction) abusing the one writer that skips validation.
payloads: POST /api/v1/setup {"app_name":"<500KB string>"}
instructions: POST /api/v1/setup with a very long app_name or login_subtitle.
Observe the value is stored without the 60/140-char cap enforced elsewhere.
execution.observed_result: Source-verified: no length check on this path; stored value re-emitted on every branded page.

remediation.strategy: Route the setup writes through saveAppName/saveLoginSubtitle (services/settings.ts) or inline the same length checks in runSetup.

likelihood.reason: Requires the broad settings:write conjunction or the bootstrap token; the marginal authority over plain branding:write (already held via expansion) is the missing cap itself.

impact.reason: Oversized stored brand value re-emitted on all pages until corrected - response inflation/mangling; no privilege gain and no new data access.

confidence.reason: Both the bounded and unbounded writers are directly readable; the prior record (flareid.branding.patch.unbounded-name-subtitle) fixes the PATCH twin only.

title: DELETE /api/v1/users/{username}/passkeys/{credential_id} lets users:write strip an administrator's passkeys - the one user-write op missing the admin-account guard
description: Every other account write in services/users.ts opens with assertMayTouchUser, which refuses non-privileged (non-'*'/non-admin-key) actors touching an account that holds an admin role. removeUserPasskey has no such check: a users:write API key or console role can delete a Super Admin's passkey credentials, weakening or locking out that administrator's second-factor posture in direct violation of the codebase's documented invariant ('an administrator's account needs *').
claimed_root_cause: src/services/users.ts:479-486 removeUserPasskey calls removePasskey directly; unlike resetUserPassword (:366), resetUserMfa (:389), setUserStatus (:344), revokeUserSessions (:402), revokeUserAppAccess (:428), deleteUser (:445) and sendUserLink (:465), it never calls assertMayTouchUser. The API route src/api/users.ts:326-332 exposes it under users:write.

trace.description: Reachable by any key or delegated role holding users:write - the ordinary directory-administration scope, minted without admin authority.
Resolves the user by username and calls removeUserPasskey(apiCtx(c), user, credential_id) - apiCtx.privileged is false for a non-admin key, but nothing downstream checks it.
removePasskey(env, user.id, credentialId) deletes the webauthn credential row for any user id, admin or not.

evidence.description: removeUserPasskey body: lookup, removePasskey, audit - no assertMayTouchUser call, in contrast to every sibling function.
resetUserMfa - the adjacent credential-stripping operation - begins with await assertMayTouchUser(ctx, id).
assertMayTouchUser: 'Changing an account that holds an admin role needs a Super Admin (an admin API key).'
The API's own contract documented on /users/{username}/invite: 'An administrator's account needs `*`.'

reason: Verifier v-api: assertMayTouchUser IS present as the first statement of removeUserPasskey (services/users.ts:480); the claimed missing guard is a misread. No boundary crossed.

title: device_codes.user_id is a bare users(id) reference absent from deleteUserStatements - any decided device code makes its user undeletable (and self-defends: the session revocation in the same batch rolls back too)
description: migrations/0033_device_flow.sql:12 declares `user_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id)` on device_codes with no ON DELETE action. deleteUserStatements (sessions.ts:143-169) - the one canonical set of per-user cleanup statements used by every user-deletion path (admin console/service deleteUser at services/users.ts:450, SCIM DELETE /scim/v2/Users/:id at scim-server.ts:511, replace-mode directory import at directory-import.ts:255, sample-data wipe at admin.ts:1009) - deletes from 14 tables but omits device_codes. The users DELETE is the last statement in the batch (sessions.ts:168), so whenever any device_codes row references the user the final DELETE hits a foreign-key violation and the ENTIRE batch rolls back atomically - including the session, token and credential deletions that would have disabled the account. Rows gain user_id when the device flow is approved or denied (device.ts:187 'UPDATE device_codes SET status = ?, user_id = ?'), expire after 600s (device.ts:34), and are only removed by the hourly cleanup (cleanup.ts:68 'DELETE FROM device_codes WHERE expires_at < ?'). title: SP metadata refresh accumulates signing certificates without bound, and a hostile publisher pins its SP into the hourly refresh set via validUntil
description: refreshSpMetadata's 'monotonic' merge unions every X509Certificate listed in each fetched metadata document into saml_service_providers.signing_certs and never removes or caps them (sp-metadata.ts:253). Each HTTP-Redirect signature verification then walks the whole list - every entry costs an X509Certificate parse, a crypto.subtle.importKey and a crypto.subtle.verify (authn-request.ts:177-182) - so per-request CPU for /saml/sso and /saml/slo grows linearly with the accumulated count, and the signing_certs JSON column grows unboundedly in D1. A hostile or compromised metadata publisher can mint fresh certificates each document (~100 certs fit under the 256 KB doc cap) and additionally set validUntil in the past: the refresh-selection OR clause (sp-metadata.ts:225) then re-selects that SP on every hourly cron run regardless of metadata_last_refreshed_at, accelerating accumulation ~24x over the intended daily cadence. Over time signed-request verification becomes the dominant per-request cost until SSO/SLO for that SP effectively stops working inside the Worker's CPU budget.
root_cause: The refresh merge treats certificate accumulation as always-safe rollover: `certs: [...new Set([...storedCerts, ...meta.signingCerts])]` (src/lib/saml/sp-metadata.ts:253) has no count or byte ceiling, and the refresh-selection predicate `metadata_valid_until IS NOT NULL AND metadata_valid_until < ?` (sp-metadata.ts:225) trusts attacker-supplied validUntil to control how often the document is re-fetched.
intended_behavior: Signing-certificate rollover should tolerate a small bound (e.g. keep N most recent certs, or cap the stored list) so a metadata publisher cannot grow per-request verification cost indefinitely, and refresh cadence should be governed by server-side state (last_refreshed) rather than publisher-supplied validUntil alone.

trace.description: Hourly cron re-selects any SP whose stored metadata_valid_until lies in the past, OR-ing that condition with the daily last_refreshed gate - a publisher that sets validUntil in the past pins its row into every hourly run.
signing_certs is rewritten as stored ∪ fetched with dedup by PEM string only - no count or byte cap; every fresh cert the publisher invents is retained forever.
meta.validUntil is persisted verbatim, feeding the attacker-controlled re-selection condition on the next cron run.

Every SSO/SLO request presenting a Signature iterates all stored certs, each costing X509Certificate parse + importKey + RSASSA verify; runtime grows linearly with accumulated cert count until requests exceed CPU budget.

evidence.description: Append-only union: certs never removed or capped.
validUntil < now re-selects the row every cron run even when last_refreshed is fresh.
256 KB metadata cap still admits ~100+ certificates per document.

verifyRedirectSignature loops spSigningCerts(sp) - the accumulated list - per request.

title: ssf_outbox dead-letter rows are never deleted - every emitted event leaves a permanent row per dead receiver, growing D1 unboundedly
description: drainSsfOutbox() selects only rows with attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS (8); when a row exhausts retries it is never deleted, only left with attempts=8 and a last_error. emitSsfEvent() inserts one row per stream per emitted event with no cap, and purgeExpiredState() - the hourly GC for every other expiring table - has no statement for ssf_outbox. Streams deleted via the API cascade their rows away, but a live-but-dead receiver accumulates one permanent row per event forever: session revocations, credential changes and account disables each enqueue a row per stream. The rows don't starve the drain (they're filtered out before the LIMIT 50) but they grow the table and the JOIN scan monotonically.

intended_behavior: Exhausted outbox rows should be removed (after recording/stream-marking the failure) - e.g. DELETE WHERE attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS after stampeding last_error, or a cleanup statement with a retention horizon - so a dead receiver doesn't turn every event into permanent storage.

WHERE attempts < 8 - rows that reach 8 attempts are permanently invisible to delivery.
Only attempts+1 and last_error are written on failure; exhausted rows persist.
GC covers auth codes, tokens, sessions, audit, rate_limits, account_tokens, session_clients, device_codes - ssf_outbox absent.

Generate events (logins, flags, revocations); after 8 hourly drains observe ssf_outbox rows persist with attempts=8 forever.

title: POST /ssf/receive has no replay protection and accepts SETs with no aud claim - a captured signed SET re-drives session revocation and risk-flag effects indefinitely
description: receiveSet() verifies the SET signature against the registered transmitter's remote JWKS, but enforces no freshness at all: jwtVerify only validates exp/nbf when present, there is no jti dedup store, and no iat window. The aud check is conditional - `aud.length && !aud.includes(env.ISSUER_URL)` - so a SET that omits aud entirely is accepted (the project's own tests sign such SETs). Two consequences: (1) replay - any valid SET addressed to this receiver, once obtained (log capture, a second receiver relaying, debugging artifacts, transmitter fan-out), can be POSTed repeatedly forever; each replay revokes the named user's sessions and tokens again after re-login, or re-adds a 24h risk-watchlist flag after an admin clears it (flagUser upserts unconditionally). (2) audience-less SETs are wildcard credentials - a transmitter that omits aud issues SETs usable at every receiver registered for that issuer, so a SET captured anywhere its bytes transit is valid here. jose is configured without an `issuer` option but that is harmless: the JWKS is selected by the unverified iss claim from the same token, so key selection binds the claim.
root_cause: src/lib/ssf.ts:190-203 - jwtVerify with only an algorithms allowlist; aud enforcement skipped when absent (line 200-202); no jti table, no exp requirement, no iat skew check before acting on events (lines 207-229).
intended_behavior: A security event is a point-in-time signal: the receiver should require aud naming this receiver, a bounded iat, and track seen jti (or otherwise bound replay) before executing session revocation or flagging.

trace.description: Body is the SET; signature is the only authentication - no bearer token, no state check.
jwtVerify(token, transmitterJwks(iss), { algorithms: [...] }) - exp/nbf validated only if present; no issuer, audience, or maxTokenAge options.
aud checked only when present; SETs without aud pass unconditionally.
session-revoked -> revokeAllSessionsForUser + revokeTokensForUser; risk events -> flagUser (24h, upserted over any cleared flag). Replayed SETs re-execute both.

`if (aud.length && !aud.includes(env.ISSUER_URL))` - empty aud skips rejection; comment concedes 'aud, when present, must name us'.
The suite's own accepted SET has no aud and no exp, and is replayable - receives a 202.
flagUser's ON CONFLICT upsert means a replayed risk SET re-flags immediately after an admin's unflagUser - replay survives remediation.

conditions.description: Attacker must possess a previously-issued valid SET: addressed to this receiver (aud includes ISSUER_URL) or bearing no aud claim; obtainable from logs, a second receiver of the same transmitter, or support artifacts. TLS protects only in transit.
A registered transmitter must exist (admin/signals:write configures it) and must issue SETs, possibly without aud.

execution.attacker_perspective: Anonymous caller who obtained one signed SET (e.g. an aud-less SET from a shared transmitter, or this receiver's own SET captured from logs).
payloads: POST /ssf/receive with the verbatim captured SET body (JWT string), repeated at will
instructions: Capture or retain a SET accepted by this receiver (the suite's own test SET demonstrates aud-less acceptance).
POST it again after the victim re-logs in or an admin clears their watchlist flag.
Observe 202 and repeated revocation of fresh sessions/tokens, or re-flagging for a fresh 24h window.
execution.observed_result: Each replayed POST returns 202 and re-executes the event effects; nothing distinguishes first delivery from the Nth - no jti dedup and no expiry to bound the token's useful life.

remediation.strategy: At the last trusted decision point (receiveSet, before effects): require aud to contain env.ISSUER_URL (make the check unconditional, matching the SSF spec's mandatory aud), reject SETs whose iat is absent or older than a small window (e.g. 5-15 min) when a jti table is impractical, and ideally store seen (issuer, jti) pairs for the window. A comment in the code already frames aud as optional hardening; the spec makes it required.

impact.reason: Replay produces repeated targeted effects: continuous session/token revocation of a named user (persistent logout) and re-flagging after administrative clears - integrity and availability harm bounded to named users.

title: A user_emails alias may equal another account's UPN - the SSF email resolver then picks a subject with `upn = ? OR email = ? LIMIT 1` and no precedence, and JIT writes bypass validation/normalisation entirely

LIMIT 1` - both rows match and LIMIT 1 picks one with no ORDER BY, so a Security Event Token addressed to either spelling can land on the wrong account (revocation / verification / credential-change-required applied to the alias owner or shadowed to the UPN owner); (b) getUserByLoginIdentifier (src/lib/db.ts:17-27) and getUserByAnyEmail (src/lib/user-emails.ts:44-51) deterministically prefer upn/users.email, silently shadowing the alias for sign-in, recovery and SCIM correlate-by-emails (scim-mapping.ts:527).
